newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia eyes delivery of F/A-18 planes - report.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia eyes delivery of F/A-18 planes - report.

text.p: Malaysia will take delivery of four F/A-18 Hornet fighter-planes from McDonnell Douglas this week, the national Bernama news agency said in a report from Washington on Tuesday.
It said Defence Minister Syed Hamid Albar, on behalf of the Royal Malaysian Air Force, would receive the two-seater aircraft on Wednesday at St Louis, Missouri.
Malaysia has ordered eight F/A-18s as part of efforts to upgrade its air force. Delivery of all aircraft will be completed by June, Bernama said.

It quoted McDonnell Douglas officials as saying the F/A-18s were equipped with the latest technology, including the upgraded Hughes APG-73 radar and twin General Electric F404-GE-402 enhanced performance engines.

Malaysia has allocated five billion ringgit ($2.02 billion) for defence equipment purchases in its 1996-2000 five-year plan. In addition to the Hornets, it is taking delivery of 28 British Aerospace Hawk 100 and 200 fighters and 18 MiG 29s.
